summary: PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20 extracts DeMarco–Krieger–Ye, Uniform Manin–Mumford for a family of genus 2 curves (Ann. Math. 191 (2020) 949–1001). It has 53 items (3 library, 10 planned, 40 missing), 3 routes and 13 source issues. It is a careful extraction with a thorough review. Every numbered statement of the published version has an item with the right hypotheses. E1–E13 stand. Route 1 has since been carried out: the accepted ArithmeticDynamics blueprint has a node for each of its 34 items, and imports the Berkovich line, Laplacian and hybrid space from TB as route 2 intends. Eight findings, one medium and seven low. (1, medium) Item 10 and its post-review correction say the absolute Weil height on ℙ¹(ℚ̄) is not in the library. Mathlib at the pin has NumberField.absMulHeight₁ and absLogHeight₁ for any field of characteristic zero, and the accepted ArithmeticDynamics blueprint uses them as that height. DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye /7 repeats the error. (2) Item 44 cites only the definition ψ, but the torsion characterisation it states is Tau Ceti's ZSMul theorems; item 3's branching at E[2] is Tau Ceti's too. (3) Item 11's Tau Ceti canonicalHeight is relative to K, [K:ℚ]·ĥ_{E_t}; the review's claim that it has the paper's normalization is false. (4, 5) Two misprints that the review noticed but did not register: the missing r_v in 2h(x) = Σ_v |log|x|_v| (p. 990) and '(singular) curve' (p. 951). (6) An unrecorded gap in the published-only proof of Proposition 9.2: w must be taken on j_Q(X). (7) FRL10, used in the proofs of Propositions 3.2 and 3.5, is missing from prerequisites. (8) readSections still says the published version was not collated, and there is no sourceVersions list.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (issue #1127), and its review, with both post-review corrections, is by Claude Code cc-442dc5. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither, and did not touch PAPER-DEMARCO-MAVRAKI-YE-26 or the ArithmeticDynamics blueprint.

Downloaded and hashed both texts on 2026-09-30. The published Annals PDF (53 pp., SHA-256 7a4bd817…07df) matches the review's hash, and arXiv v2 (49 pp., 8fc51ac3…bab8) matches the extraction's. Read §§1–2 and 7–9 of the published version in full as text, and the statements and the proof steps the items rely on in §§3–6. Checked the page images of pp. 990 and 993. The image check matters: text extraction drops overlines, and on p. 993 it turns X(K̄) into X(K). I therefore withdrew a candidate slip there.

Compared every numbered statement of the published version with the items: Theorems 1.1, 1.5–1.8 and 1.10, Conjecture 1.4, Remarks 1.2–1.3, Propositions 1.9, 2.1–2.3, 3.2–3.6, 4.2–4.4, 5.3, 7.3, 8.3, 9.1 and 9.2, Theorems 3.1, 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, 7.1 and 8.1, Lemmas 4.1 and 6.1–6.3, Corollary 8.2, and Remark 6.4. Each has an item, and the hypotheses of items 25, 33–35, 42 and 43 match (for example b = −log|s|/log|t| ≥ 1 in Theorem 5.5, and 0 ≤ b < δ/2 in Theorem 7.1). Remark 1.11, the Kawaguchi–Silverman comparison, proves nothing the paper uses.

Re-derived: α = r/16 − r²/2 = 1/512 at r = 1/16 (Remark 6.4); the algebra of (7.6) and the choice ε′ < ε/16; the E5 bound Σ_v −r_v log η_v ≤ 4Σ(h(t_i) + h(1 − t_i)) − log c(ε′) place by place; that E7's repaired η_v adds exactly log 2, which E7's correction already states; the Jacobi model maps (x, y) ↦ (x², y) and (1/x², iy/x³) with their branch sets; |Δ_t|^{1/6} = |2|^{2/3}|t(t − 1)|^{1/3} ≥ |2| min{1, |t(t − 1)|} in the potentially good range; and the three-common-branch-value genus 2 of §9.1.

Checked E1–E13 against the published text: all stand, and the ArithmeticDynamics packet re-records them (E301, E507, E509, E701–E707) with the extraction's ids as 'known', so none is recorded twice. Went through the review's list of slips 'noted but not registered'. The missing r_v and '(singular)' are real misprints (findings 4 and 5). 'The loose factor 16' in §9.3 is a valid if generous bound (4 would do). The doubled 'on' on p. 997 is not mathematical. (2.14)'s '∖ Diag' is harmless when read as the diagonal of type I points.

Library claims at the pins: Mathlib 082e2d3 has WeierstrassCurve, WeierstrassCurve.ψ, ΨSq, j, Δ and Projectivization.logHeight. It also has NumberField.absMulHeight₁ (:137) and absLogHeight₁ (:146), which item 10 wrongly says are absent. Tau Ceti f790474 has canonicalHeight (CanonicalHeight.lean:124, relative to K), canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder (:338), naiveHeight (NaiveHeight.lean:91), and the ψ_n torsion theorems (ZSMul.lean:1071, :1084, :1128).

Routes. The stage texts of DY.1, DY.2, DY.4, DY.6, TB.0, TB.1, TB.6, RP.0 and RP.5 are in the assembled atlas (2840 stages, 8007 edges). No restructuring touches ArithmeticDynamics, TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic or RP.5, and RS-03's narrowing of RP.0 keeps the imported absolute heights. Route 1 has been carried out: all 34 of its items have nodes in the accepted ArithmeticDynamics packet (403 nodes when it was first merged, #2884 on 2026-09-24, and 415 now). That includes DY.2/archimedean-canonical-measure, DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate, DY.4/mutual-energy-metric, DY.4/zhang-inequality-on-p1, and DY.6 nodes for Propositions 2.1, 2.3 and 3.2–3.6, Theorems 3.1, 5.1–5.5, 7.1 and 8.1, Lemmas 6.1–6.3, Corollary 8.2, Propositions 8.3 and DWY16 1.4, and the standard projection. So DY.2's nonarchimedean wording did not strand the archimedean items 13 and 17. For route 2, the DY packet imports TB.0, TB.1 and TB.6 for the Berkovich line, Laplacian and hybrid space; the TB packet (30 nodes, TB.1 and TB.6 not_read) builds no second copy.

Duplication. Searched every papers/*.result.json for Arakelov–Zhang, mutual energy, Hsia, hybrid space, essential minimum, Fili, Lattès, adelic metrics and equidistribution. PAPER-DEMARCO-MAVRAKI-YE-26 routes Yuan–Zhang's quasi-projective fundamental inequality (/33–35) to ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeightsPartII and its essential-minimum items to ArithmeticDynamicsPartIIBifurcation. These are different statements from Zhang's 1995 inequality on ℙ¹ (item 23), so there is no duplicate. Its item /7 repeats item 10's wrong library note (finding 1). The atlas has no complex-dynamics roadmap competing for items 13, 17 and 29.

Route 3. Its brief coalesces with the Part II proposed by PAPER-YUAN-26, PAPER-GAO-GE-KUHNE-26, PAPER-DIMITROV-GAO-HABEGGER-21 and PAPER-GAO-HABEGGER-19. Checked the brief's claims about Proposition 9.1 against pp. 995–996: the Jacobi model, the maps to E₁ and E₂, the three common branch values, Φ of degree 4 with three nontrivial kernel elements, and Weierstrass points as the six preimages. Its 'Acceptance' clause, that Theorems 1.1 and 1.10 follow from Kühne and Gao–Ge–Kühne, is plausible, since Φ*L_D should be algebraically equivalent to 2Θ. I did not verify it and do not record it as a finding.

Prerequisites: compared the paper's 38 references with the twelve listed prerequisites and with where each reference is used. FRL10 is used in two proofs and is missing (finding 7). DF16 and BP05 are cited only as alternatives, and KS09 only in Remark 1.11.

findings.claim: Item 10's note says that 'the absolute height on ℙ¹(ℚ̄) used by the paper is not in the library'. The review's post-review correction, which set the status from library to planned, says there is 'no Q̄ version'. Both are false at the pin. Mathlib 082e2d3 defines the absolute multiplicative and logarithmic heights of an algebraic number in any field of characteristic zero, ℚ̄ included, normalised through ℚ⟮x⟯. With h(∞) = 0, this is the paper's h on ℙ¹(ℚ̄). The accepted ArithmeticDynamics blueprint builds on exactly this declaration. So RP.0 is now asked to plan a height the library already has, and the DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye extraction carries the same wrong note. The library does lack the absolute height of a tuple, which the paper's naive height h(t₁, t₂) on 𝔸²(ℚ̄) needs, and the identity 2h(x) = Σ_v r_v |log|x|_v|.

findings.claim: Item 44 says the torsion images π(E_t[n]) 'are cut out by polynomials in (x, t)'. §8.2 uses this in the form 'x ∈ π(E_t^tors) for all t … as it is a root of a division polynomial'. That needs the theorem that ψ_n vanishes at a point exactly when n kills it. The item cites only the definition `WeierstrassCurve.ψ`. Mathlib at the pin has no such theorem: its DivisionPolynomial directory holds only Basic.lean and Degree.lean. Tau Ceti at the pin proves both directions over any field, and also that 2-torsion is exactly the vanishing of ψ₂. That last fact is the 'branched exactly over π(E_t[2])' claim of item 3, which also cites only `WeierstrassCurve`. The statuses are right, but the citations do not support the statements.

findings.claim: Item 11 names the paper's ĥ_{E_t}, the absolute Néron–Tate height with ĥ_{E_t}(P) = ½ ĥ_t(π(P)) on E_t(ℚ̄). It cites Tau Ceti's `canonicalHeight`, which is the height relative to the field. It is ½ lim h_K(x(2ⁿP))/4ⁿ, where h_K is the logarithmic height of Mathlib's AdmissibleAbsValues on the number field K, the sum over all places with local degrees and no division by [K:ℚ]. So canonicalHeight = [K:ℚ]·ĥ_{E_t} on E_t(K), and it changes with K. The review nevertheless says that `canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder` 'has the normalization ĥ_{E_t} = ½ ĥ_t∘π that §9.4 needs'. That is false. The accepted ArithmeticDynamics blueprint records the factor. The zero locus and the quadratic-form property do not depend on the factor, so the library status can stand. But neither the item nor the review states the normalization, and item 11 has no link to where the absolute comparison is planned.

findings.claim: An unrecorded misprint. The proof of Theorem 7.1 says: 'Since the logarithmic Weil height satisfies 2h(x) = Σ_v |log|x|_v|'. The weights r_v = [K_v:ℚ_v]/[K:ℚ] are missing. Unweighted, the identity is false: for K = ℚ(√2) and x = 2, the two real places and the ramified place above 2 each give log 2, a total of 3 log 2, while 2h(2) = 2 log 2. With the weights (½, ½, 1) the total is 2 log 2. The display that follows is right only with the weights. The review saw this and did not register it ('Noted but not registered: … the missing r_v on p.41'). §18 says mistakes 'are recorded, never silently corrected'. Item 10's statement prints the corrected identity without citing an issue.
findings.evidence: Published p. 990 (page image checked): 'Since the logarithmic Weil height satisfies 2 h(x) = Σ_v |log|x|_v|, we thus obtain ĥ_{t_i} · h_{F,η} ≤ b + 2ε′(h(t_i) + h(t_i − 1)) + …'. arXiv v2 p. 41 has the same sentence. §2.1 (published p. 955) defines r_v := [K_v:ℚ_v]/[K:ℚ]. findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry); items PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20/2 and /5; source: §1, after Conjecture 1.4, published p. 951 (arXiv v2 p. 2, after Conjecture 1.3)
findings.claim: An unrecorded misprint, also noted by the review but not registered ('"(singular) curve" after Conjecture 1.3'). The source says that for any two standard projections with π₁(E₁[2]) ≠ π₂(E₂[2]), the diagonal of ℙ¹ × ℙ¹ 'lifts to a (singular) curve C ⊂ E₁ × E₂ … with normalization of genus g ≥ 2'. C = (π₁ × π₂)^{-1}(D) is singular exactly over the common branch values of π₁ and π₂. Near a point where both project to a common branch value, C is u² = w², a node. Where only one of them does, it is u² = v, smooth. So when the two branch sets are disjoint, which the hypothesis allows, C is smooth and is its own normalization. Riemann–Hurwitz for the degree-4 map to D, with 8 branch values each carrying two simple ramification points, gives 2g − 2 = −8 + 16, so g = 5. The conclusion g ≥ 2 stands. Only 'singular' is wrong in general.
findings.evidence: Published p. 951: 'The finiteness of the set π₁(E₁^tors) ∩ π₂(E₂^tors), under the assumption that π₁(E₁[2]) ≠ π₂(E₂[2]), follows from the main theorem of Raynaud in [Ray83]; indeed, the diagonal in P¹ × P¹ lifts to a (singular) curve C ⊂ E₁ × E₂ via π₁ × π₂ with normalization of genus g ≥ 2 [BT07].' arXiv v2 p. 2 is the same. §9.1 (published p. 995) itself computes the three-common-values case: 'each branch point the image of two points in X, each of multiplicity two. By Riemann-Hurwitz, the genus of X is 2'. REV-PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20.md, 'Noted but not registered': '"(singular) curve" after Conjecture 1.3'.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20.result.json: sourceIssues (no entry); item PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20/53 (note); source: proof of Proposition 9.2, §9.5, published p. 997 (not in arXiv v2)
findings.claim: An unrecorded gap in the published-only proof of Proposition 9.2. The proposition asserts a point of order ≥ N in j_P(X) ∩ J(X)^tors. The proof takes 'w a preimage in J(X) of the point (x₀, x₀) in ℙ¹ × ℙ¹ under the map (π × π) ∘ Φ' and concludes 'Then w has order at least N'. Such preimages form 16 points of J(X): four points of E_{t₁} × E_{t₂} over (x₀, x₀), each with four Φ-preimages. The proof never puts w on j_Q(X), and without that it does not prove the proposition. The step is easily repaired. Φ ∘ j_Q(X) = (π × π)^{-1}(D) contains (P_{t₁}, P_{t₂}), so some w ∈ j_Q(X) has Φ(w) = (P_{t₁}, P_{t₂}). That w is torsion of order ≥ lcm(ord P_{t₁}, ord P_{t₂}) ≥ N. Item 53's note makes this repair ('a point of j_Q(X) over (x₀, x₀)') without a source issue.
findings.evidence: Published p. 997: 'From Proposition 9.1, we know that X is of genus 2 and lies in L₂, and there is a Weierstrass point Q ∈ X so that j_Q(X) maps to the curve C under a degree-four isogeny Φ : J(X) → E_{t₁} × E_{t₂}. Let w be a preimage in J(X) of the point (x₀, x₀) in P¹ × P¹ under the map (π × π) ∘ Φ. Then w has order at least N.' Proposition 9.2 (p. 997): 'the intersection j_P(X) ∩ J(X)^tors contains a point of order ≥ N'. Proposition 9.1 (p. 995): 'Φ ∘ j_Q(X) = (π₁ × π₂)^{-1} D'. Item 53 note: 'a point of j_Q(X) over (x₀, x₀) maps under the isogeny Φ to a pair of torsion points of order ≥ N'.
findings.fix: Add source issue PAPER-DEMARCO-KRIEGER-YE-20/E16: kind gap, affects nothing, known new, searched as in E14. It is in the published version only. Locator: proof of Proposition 9.2, §9.5, p. 997. Printed: 'Let w be a preimage in J(X) of the point (x₀, x₀) in P¹ × P¹ under the map (π × π) ∘ Φ. Then w has order at least N.' Correction: 'Since Φ ∘ j_Q(X) = (π × π)^{-1}(D) contains (P_{t₁}, P_{t₂}), choose w ∈ j_Q(X) with Φ(w) = (P_{t₁}, P_{t₂}). Then w is torsion of order at least N, and w ∈ j_Q(X) ∩ J(X)^tors with P = Q.' Reason: as above. Cite E16 in item 53's note. Re-run check_paper.py.

findings.claim: The proof of Proposition 3.2 takes its key step from Favre–Rivera-Letelier 2010. That step is that the interval I is totally invariant and f_t acts on it by a tent map of degree 2. The proof of Proposition 3.5 follows the same computations ('We proceed as in the computations of [FRL10, §5.1]'). Item 26 cites it as [FRL2, §5.1]. The paper is not in the extraction's twelve prerequisites. It is not in papers.json or among the ArithmeticDynamics packet's sources, and nothing else in the repository cites it. §16 lists in prerequisites 'the papers this one builds on that the atlas does not yet cover'. (DeMarco–Faber 2016 and Baker–Petsche 2005 are cited only as alternatives to a listed source or a stated direct calculation, so they are not needed.)
